articles.title: Colts announce firing of general manager Chris Ballard after loss to Titans, DeForest Buckner criticism
articles.summary: Chris Ballard is out after nearly a decade as the Colts' general manager.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are moving on from general manager Chris Ballard. The team announced Monday that Ballard was relieved from his duties.

In a statement, team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said the team's standard "is to compete for championships." She added that she believes "a change in leadership is necessary to meet that standard."

"I am grateful to Chris for his years of service to the Colts and for everything he poured into this organization. He cared deeply about our team and our community, and we wish Chris and his family all the best. "As I said at the start of the season, the sense of urgency has never been higher. Our standard is to compete for championships, and I believe a change in leadership is necessary to meet that standard. "Making this change during the season was a deliberate decision. Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now. We will conduct a thorough search for our next general manager and take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of this organization. "I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for this season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve, and win football games."

"I am grateful to Chris for his years of service to the Colts and for everything he poured into this organization. He cared deeply about our team and our community, and we wish Chris and his family all the best.

"As I said at the start of the season, the sense of urgency has never been higher. Our standard is to compete for championships, and I believe a change in leadership is necessary to meet that standard.

"Making this change during the season was a deliberate decision. Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now. We will conduct a thorough search for our next general manager and take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of this organization.

"I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for this season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve, and win football games."

The decision comes with the team sitting at 2-4 after six weeks. It also comes after the Colts fell to the previously winless Tennessee Titans in Week 6. After the contest, Colts star DeForest Buckner expressed his frustration with the organization, saying he was "sick and tired of the same song and dance every year."

Ballard has been responsible for that "song and dance" since 2017. While he's experienced some moments of excellence — drafting Shaquille Leonard and Jonathan Taylor and signing Daniel Jones on the cheap in 2025 — he's also experienced some high-profile misses, such as drafting Anthony Richardson, hiring Jeff Saturday, trading a pair of first-round picks for Sauce Gardner and inking Jones to a two-year, $88 million extension ahead of the 2026 season.

Through six games, that extension looks regrettable. Jones has regressed after a promising 2025. This season, he's completed a career-low 59.6 percent of his passes, and has just four touchdowns against six interceptions, two of which came in the team's Week 6 loss.

The trade for Gardner has not only lacked results for Indianapolis on the field — he's yet to record an interception for the Colts and hasn't matched his All-Pro play in New York — it cost the Colts their first-round pick in April and (barring a trade) will mean they won't have a first-round pick in the 2027 draft, either.

The team's next general manager will be tasked with figuring out whether Jones deserves to remain the Colts' starter next season. Even if that answer is yes, finding a long-term quarterback is almost certainly a priority for a team that has been scrambling for stability at the position ever since the surprising retirement of former No. 1 overall pick Andrew Luck in 2019.

articles.title: The Cleveland Browns are good. What do we all do now?
articles.summary: At 4-2, the Browns are in first place in their division, a spot they haven't been in this late in a season since 2014.
articles.body:
There are certain truths we hold to be self-evident: The sun rises in the east. Star Wars movies were better when you were a kid. And the Cleveland Browns will always, always be terrible.

So what happens when one of our bedrock truths turns out to be wrong? What happens when — I can't believe I'm writing this — the Cleveland Browns turn out to be good?

As of Week 6, the Cleveland Browns lead the AFC North — by tiebreaker, at least — with a record of 4-2. That's better than the defending champion Seahawks, better than the supposed super-team Rams, better than the entire NFC South and East. This is the latest the Browns have been in first place in a season since 2014, one of those stats that makes you cringe because it even has to be said.

How did this happen? Well, nobody's going to like the answer. Coming into the season, the verdict on Cleveland was that this was a donut of a team , blessed with talent on both sides of the ball but lacking that essential core — i.e., a quarterback. This problem has haunted Cleveland for decades , of course, but it became particularly acute when Cleveland's front office piled up draft picks and then, shockingly, used them wisely.

Shedeur Sanders wasn't the one. Dillon Gabriel wasn't the one. Joe Flacco wasn't the one. As it turned out, the one quarterback able to lead the Cleveland Browns to victory is the quarterback nobody wants to lead the Cleveland Browns to victory.

Deshaun Watson, it turns out, is the answer to Cleveland's quarterback troubles. Of course.

Watson, who's been accused of dozens of counts of sexual assault and settled 20 claims, is just about the last person any organization would want as the face of their team. Were this virtually any other workplace, Watson would have been kicked to the curb and forgotten years ago. But the NFL has a forgiveness blind spot for players who are just too talented to disregard, and Watson has set up camp in that blind spot.

Regardless of the court of public opinion — and the Browns, among other teams, made it clear they don't recognize the authority of that court when they pursued Watson in the first place — Watson has met all the terms of his employment with the NFL. That means all his past "adversity" — the euphemism announcers are now employing to sanitize the many allegations against him — will remain in his past. And as distasteful as it may be to a swath of NFL fans, Watson is forcing the league to consider him in football terms, not social ones.

From a football standpoint, Watson has been a qualified success this season. He's not dominating games, but he's not losing them, either, which in the current NFL is enough. He has seven touchdowns against two interceptions this season, with a passer rating of 92.0 and a completion rate of 63.8 percent. That's not good enough to reign, but it's good enough to survive.

The Browns are coalescing around Watson. The defense lost Myles Garrett via trade, but remains strong enough to contain opposing offenses. Against Baltimore on Sunday, for instance, Cleveland's defense gave up 10 points in the first quarter, but nothing the rest of the game. That allowed Watson and the offense to plod along, turning a crucial Derrick Henry fumble into a touchdown and kicking just two field goals, including a walkoff game-winner.

The Browns are reveling in the moment … for the moment. "I'm going to enjoy tonight," first-year head coach Todd Monken said after the win. "And that's what you have to do in the NFL. These are the nights that you don't ever want to end, because tomorrow it's on to the next game."

Here's the good news for Cleveland: the "next game" is woeful Tennessee. After that, the Steelers, the Saints, the Texans — on and on, winnable game after winnable game. The only current division leader on the Browns' remaining schedule: the NFC East's Giants. Not exactly a fearsome slate.

This most definitely isn't the way you want to build a team, with a radioactive quarterback and a defense that relies more on opportunity than overwhelming force. But it's working for Cleveland, and in a year where there's no one dominant team, slow and steady keeps you in the race.

No, we're not saying the Cleveland Browns will go 15-2 this season. But we're saying there's a non-zero chance they could. And that should concern all of us. Because if the Cleveland Browns are now good, what can we even believe in anymore?

articles.title: Caleb Williams reveals Keanu Reeves reached out before Falcons game, giving Bears fans an unexpected Hollywood connection
articles.summary: Caleb Williams had more than football on his mind before the Chicago Bears faced the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6.
articles.body: Caleb Williams had more than football on his mind before the Chicago Bears faced the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6. The quarterback, returning after missing three games with a hamstring injury, caught fans' attention with a John Wick-inspired Instagram profile picture and the caption “I’m Inevitable.” The reference had a surprising connection to Hollywood. During an appearance on NBC's Sunday Night Football, Williams revealed that Keanu Reeves, the actor behind the famous action franchise, had contacted him before the game. The message offered an unexpected boost ahead of a crucial return, and Williams followed it with a strong performance in Atlanta.Caleb Williams explains Keanu Reeves' message before Falcons gameWilliams' John Wick reference was more than a social media joke. The Bears quarterback had been watching the films during the week, drawing inspiration from the character's mindset as he prepared to return from injury.Speaking with Sunday Night Football host Maria Taylor, Williams explained how the connection came about.“I was watching John Wick for this week, a couple of his movies I watched, he actually reached out which was really cool,” Williams said. “He was a fan, and [I’m a] big fan of him, and so that was my profile picture. The mindset of him is also why it was my profile and that I’m inevitable. That’s always my mentality every single day that I get to live and breathe.”Reeves' message made the moment even more memorable for Williams, who has never been shy about expressing confidence in his abilities. The actor reportedly called him a “beast,” offering encouragement before the quarterback returned to action.Williams admitted he did not spend much time thinking about the exchange because his attention remained on the game.“He just reached out and he was a fan and [called me] a beast and things like that and it was kind of simple. I was so locked in this week I didn’t fully read into it,” Williams explained.That response says something about Williams' priorities. The celebrity connection made for an entertaining story, but his immediate focus was getting back on the field and helping Chicago win.Caleb Williams delivers strong performance as Bears beat FalconsThe quarterback gave Chicago plenty to feel good about in his return. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and one touchdown as the Bears secured a victory over Atlanta on October 18.Those numbers were particularly encouraging given the time he had missed. Sitting out three consecutive games can disrupt a quarterback's rhythm, timing with receivers and feel for the offense. Williams showed little sign of rust, completing passes efficiently and finding open targets throughout the contest.Bears head coach Ben Johnson also praised the quarterback's preparation after his extended absence.“It’s the biggest injury layoff he’s ever had. He came in my office early in the week wanting to push it and see where he was at. He did a great job downloading the game plan, finding open guys, and delivering good football. Super proud of him,” Johnson said.Johnson's comments highlighted an important part of Williams' return. His performance was not simply about throwing for more than 300 yards. He also had to absorb the game plan, regain his timing and make sound decisions despite limited time on the field.The victory also gave Chicago an encouraging sign about Williams' recovery. While one game cannot settle every question about his health, his accuracy and command against Atlanta offered reasons for optimism.Reeves' unexpected message added a memorable detail to the week, but Williams' work on the field gave the story its real payoff. His “I’m Inevitable” caption now has a performance to support it. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ parents Ed and Darla Rodgers sell 5,300 sq ft California home for $1.68M as Steelers QB’s Wisconsin mansion remains unsold
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers’ parents, Ed and Darla Rodgers, sold their longtime California property for $1.68 million.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers’ parents, Ed and Darla Rodgers, sold their longtime California property for $1.68 million. They secured a significant profit on the property they purchased almost two decades ago.As per Realtor, Ed and Darla Rodgers’ five-bedroom mansion in Chico, California, was sold just weeks after being listed on the market. They initially listed the mansion for $1.75 million but eventually sold it for $1.68 million, still a significant increase over its purchase price.The Rodgers family sold their property just as Aaron was navigating another season with the Pittsburgh Steelers in May 2026. Their son, too, has his own Wisconsin mansion on the market.Aaron Rodgers’ parents Ed and Darla Rodgers’ California mansionAaron Rodgers’ parents, Ed and Darla Rodgers, purchased the California property in 2007 for $306,000. The mansion was bought two years after Rodgers was drafted by the Green Bay Packers. The 5,300-square-foot residence boasts a Victorian Craftsman style and sits on over 3 acres.Among its features are smart home technology, a custom theater room, a separate one-bedroom apartment, a 3-car garage, and a hot tub.According to the property’s listing, the residence boasts timeless finishes, indoor-outdoor living spaces, and thoughtfully designed areas that offer the family living there - the comfort of a home.Rodgers spent his childhood with his siblings in Chico. His father played football for the Chico State Wildcats. Aaron attended Pleasant Valley High School. He played college football for the California Golden Bears. By the time Rodgers’ parents purchased the Chico property, he had already left for the NFL.Aaron Rodgers’ Wisconsin mansionAaron Rodgers’ parents’ California mansion was sold, but his own Wisconsin mansion still remains on the market. The Hobart mansion was listed for $3.7 million in November 2025.The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback listed the Wisconsin mansion for $2.8 million in 2024 but withdrew it due to sentimental attachment to the area.Rodgers purchased the massive property for just over $1.7 million in 2015, when he played for the Green Bay Packers. The 10,500 sq-ft property sits on a 5.32-acre lot. Lush greenery and numerous trees surround it, providing desirable privacy.The luxurious abode boasts a billiard room with a bar, a brick theater with built-in seating and a wet bar, a fitness room, a steam shower, a wine cellar, and a changing room. Exteriorly, the mansion features a patio with a fire pit, a greenhouse, and tennis and pickleball courts.Aaron Rodgers’ rift with familyIn 2016, Aaron Rodgers’ younger brother Jordan Rodgers appeared on The Bachelorette. Jordan spoke about the distance between Aaron and the rest of the family. He expressed sadness over their strained relationship and hoped for reconciliation.In 2017, Aaron’s father, Ed, told The New York Times that Aaron had not spoken to the family since 2014. He hoped that their relationship could improve. In 2024, Aaron spoke about his family in the Netflix documentary, Aaron Rodgers: Enigma.The quarterback said losing his family connection was heartbreaking for him. He largely kept the matter private.Then in July 2026, Aaron posted five snapshots of his beautiful family, parents - Ed and Darla Rodgers and brother Luke, on his Instagram. A user commented on the photos, “his wife definitely made this [family reunion] happen.”Aaron is married to Brittani, whom he met in 2017. “In 2017, I met my wife, and at the time, she was leaving the States and going back to Europe.And my biggest regret is not begging her to stay or proposing right there, because that sent me right there into a tailspin of what I can be accused of as a partner in a relationship,” Aaron told Pittsburgh teammate Cam Heyward in September 2026.Aaron met his wife Brittani while she was living in Austin, Texas, after attending the University of Texas at Austin. He also credited her with helping him reunite with his family.“A year ago, even two years ago, five years ago for sure, I would have said, ‘Naah, I’m never going to reconcile,’” Aaron said. “My wife deserves a lot of the credit for that just to be able to get to that point to think about having the conversations, she was a big part of that.And not that she was pushing anything; she wasn’t. It was more, and you guys can probably relate to this, when you’re loved by someone in such an unconditional, beautiful, pure way, it changes your perspective on all of your relationships around that; that becomes your anchor point.Well, if I can be made to feel like this by this person, I feel like it opens up your heart in an even deeper way that I never experienced before.”Aaron’s family attended the Week 5 game to cheer him up. This surely feels like his final year. His team, the Pittsburgh Steelers, won against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 19-26 in Week 6. articles.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts playing with blood clots deserves heavy scrutiny
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts played despite reportedly not sleeping for 36 hours before kickoff. How?
articles.body:
In the leadup to the Philadelphia Eagles game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Oct. 11, doctors advised Jalen Hurts not to sleep because it was too risky, according to multiple reports from NFL insiders . Yet, the Philadelphia Eagles let him play football.

On Monday, more details were reported on Hurts' blood clot issue, which is expected to keep him out for the rest of the season, according to ESPN . The new details were so jarring that the NFL will have to conduct an investigation into who knew what, when it was known and the process that led to Hurts playing against the Jacksonville Jaguars. ( According to Pro Football Talk , the league was in communication with the Eagles over Hurts' health before the Week 5 game.)

Here are the details, based on multiple reports Monday: Before the Eagles played the Jaguars in Week 5, Hurts was in the hospital until 4 a.m. due to the clot in his leg and didn't sleep "because sleep was a risk," according to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport. Hurts played anyway. Initially, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported that "doctors told [Hurts] not to sleep as a precaution, so he had been awake for roughly 36 hours" by the time he played in London. Later on Monday, Pelissero walked back his initial report , saying, "Hurts was up until early Sunday morning getting evaluated at a hospital, he was able to sleep upon rejoining the team and the Eagles set aside a room for him at the stadium. Videos from the stadium show Hurts coming onto the field just before kickoff and he felt rested enough to play."

Even if Hurts wanted to play, and even if medical personnel said he could, there is a clear and obvious risk in a player who was up all night due to a blood clot being on a football field. Common sense and concern for safety should have taken over at some point, which head coach Nick Sirianni said happened.

"We get medical information from our guys," Sirianni told reporters Tuesday . "Our players health is first and foremost. I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical folks in every situation. I have full faith in them. It's not just me who has major care for our players, it's them as well."

What's more, after further evaluation the clots have been found not to be isolated to Hurts' leg, as initially diagnosed prior to the Oct. 11 game. More clots were found in Hurts' lungs, a serious condition that required emergency medical attention and why Hurts is reportedly being shut down for the rest of the season.

Football is a competitive business. Those involved can get caught up with that and make rash and selfish decisions when it comes to allowing players to play.

Even in that scope, having Hurts play against the Jaguars seems overly dangerous.

Even after he was cleared to play (the Eagles said last week that doctors and their medical staff said he was cleared), the coaching staff led by Sirianni had to make the decision to have him active — if Sirianni didn't know the seriousness of the issue, that's another chapter to the story — and let him play on no sleep, dealing with a frightening medical issue, against the Jaguars.

Maybe Hurts insisted on playing, because that's what football players have been trained to do — play. But sometimes they need to be saved from themselves. Playing through a sprained ankle is much different than playing through blood clots.

The NFL will have to look into how this reportedly happened. It's a horrific look for everyone involved. It's nothing to be celebrated.

Hurts played in what ended up being a last-second loss to the Jaguars on Oct. 11. Four days later, news broke that Hurts was ruled out for the Eagles' Week 6 game due to a "superficial blood clot" in his calf. The statement from the team said that "our medical staff and doctors in London" concluded Hurts could play. So he did. And then he practiced last Wednesday when he got back home. Since then he was ruled out, put on injured reserve and then news Monday said he'd be out for the season. Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

Based on what we know now, and the treatment he got in London, that entire timeline is stunning. The Eagles and Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn put out a joint statement Monday.

Even if Hurts was cleared, the Eagles playing him in a game after he reportedly had no sleep and was dealing with blood clots deserves further explanation from the Eagles, otherwise everyone involved looks surprisingly cavalier about a player's safety. Everyone, from team owner Jeffrey Lurie on down, should have been involved in the decision on a superstar quarterback playing despite blood clots.

The Eagles are fortunate the situation didn't become more serious during the game. As is, now that more of the puzzle has been revealed after being kept secret for more than a week, a whole new set of questions has to be asked.

articles.title: Sean Payton says Broncos have no plans to make quarterback change amid Bo Nix's rough start
articles.summary: Bo Nix has just six touchdowns in six games this season.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos have no plans to make a change at quarterback amid Bo Nix's rocky start. Head coach Sean Payton flatly said "no" when asked whether the team would consider going with another option at the position, per ESPN.

Payton added that some of Nix's issues are likely the result of the entire Broncos' offense struggling so far. Payton said he believes Nix's play will improve naturally as the rest of the offense shows improvement.

"[Nix is] going to become the by-product of all of the finer things that get improved, the improved play of our offensive line, the more efficient we are relative to balance running the football, and that's, you know, that's our job as coaches here.''

Payton also complimented Nix's ability to "climb through adversity," saying that was a reason the team selected him in the 2024 NFL Draft.

Through six games, Nix has tossed just six touchdowns against three interceptions. His 60.3 percent completion percentage is currently a career-low, as are his passing and rushing yards per game. In four of the team's six games, Nix has failed to eclipse 200 yards passing.

Despite that, the Broncos sit at 4-2 on the season. The team's defense has played a significant role in that, holding opponents to 17 points or fewer in three of the Broncos' four victories.

While Nix's play has been problematic, the entire Broncos' offense has struggled in 2026. The team's rushing attack has been held under 100 yards in four of its first six games this season. Last year, the Broncos experienced just five games with under 100 yards rushing over the course of the regular season.

None of the team's pass catchers have emerged either, with running back RJ Harvey leading the team in receptions. Newly acquired wideout Jaylen Waddle has one game with over 100 receiving yards. In the other five, he's averaging just 18 receiving yards per game.

The Broncos quickly recognized the offense was an issue this season. After just four games, Payton reclaimed play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb. The Broncos won the two games in which Payton called offensive plays, though the team's offense has yet to show meaningful improvement since the shift.

Getting the Broncos' offense back on track would go a long way toward the team returning to its status as a legitimate Super Bowl contender. The team has already shown it's capable of putting up a winning record while the offense struggles. Getting the team to put points on the board at a league-average rate could get the team back to last season's heights, when the Broncos went 14-3 and earned the top playoff seed in the AFC.

articles.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts reportedly out for 2026 season after being diagnosed with blood clots in lungs
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the 2026 season due to the issue.
articles.body:
After the Philadelphia Eagles officially placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve over the weekend, the team and his agent released a joint statement on his condition Monday, saying the quarterback is dealing with deep vein thrombosis as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli.

While the team knew about and announced the blood clot in Hurts' leg , the bilateral pulmonary emboli is a new development for the quarterback. A bilateral pulmonary emboli involves multiple blood clots in the lungs.

As a result of that diagnosis, Hurts will be placed on blood thinners, and is unable to play football until he is fully recovered. Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and he is expected to make a "full recovery," per the joint statement .

"Over the past few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. "Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation [i.e. "blood thinners"]. During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football. "Jalen's progress is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. "We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."

In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.

"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."

While the statement did not offer a timetable for Hurts' recovery, multiple reports said he'd miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season.

The Eagles initially discovered a blood clot in Hurts' leg prior to the team's Week 5 game in London. At the time, the team determined Hurts could play in the contest. While initial reports suggested Hurts was awake for 36 hours straight ahead of the game due to recommendations from doctors, that apparently was not the case. Hurts was reportedly up until early Sunday morning being evaluated, but was allowed to sleep after rejoining the team, per NFL Network's Tom Pelissero.

Hurts threw for 220 yards and a score in the 19-17 loss .

Hurts was able to practice without restriction the following Wednesday, but a follow-up ultrasound revealed "movement in the small blood clot." Because of that, Hurts was ruled out in Week 6.

With Hurts sidelined, the Eagles turned to Tanner McKee in Week 6. McKee went 26 of 45 with 215 yards and one passing touchdown in the team's 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers in his third career NFL start.

McKee will presumably take over as the team's starter moving forward as long as Hurts is out.

Following four straight losses, the Eagles sit at 2-4 entering Week 7. Digging the team out of that hole could prove difficult for McKee, especially if star running back Saquon Barkley remains out due to a hamstring injury. Barkley has already missed two games due to the issue.

articles.title: Adonai Mitchell and 3 Other Week 7 Fantasy Waiver Wire Adds No One Is Talking About
articles.summary: Some players who have not drawn a ton of attention in fantasy football that fantasy managers should be looking to pick up on waivers this week.
articles.body:
Headed into Week 7 of the fantasy football season , there are a ton of players who are flying under the radar in this week's fantasy waiver wire pool. With that, here are four deep fantasy sleepers worth taking a chance on adding off fantasy waivers this week.

New York Jets rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. had a great outing in Week 6 against the New England Patriots. He logged six receptions on seven targets for 103 yards and a TD. In PPR formats for the week, he ranked as WR6, without Monday night's game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Washington Commanders being accounted for.

So, headed into Week 7, Cooper Jr. is probably on the majority of fantasy managers' minds when thinking of who to add off waivers. However, another Jets WR may actually have a better fantasy outlook for the rest of 2026, than him. That being Adonai Mitchell.

Cooper Jr. in Week 6 played in 82% of snaps. He could see his snap share deplete immediately upon the return of Mitchell, who is out with an injury and is listed as week-to-week.

Prior to getting hurt, Mitchell had an encouraging performance in the last game he was available, against the Green Bay Packers in Week 2. He had six receptions for 63 yards on a team-high 12 targets. That, compounded with how he played in the final stretch of the 2025 season, makes him a great player to take a chance on in fantasy. In ESPN fantasy leagues, he is currently rostered by 17.4% of teams.

The New York Giants' passing offense continues to really only target two guys: TE Isaiah Likely and WR Malik Nabers. If their production does inevitably get spread out, the next player in line to get a notable target share should be WR Malachi Fields.

In Week 6, the listed WR2 on the Giants roster played in a season-high 94% of snaps. That helped him get a season-high in targets, logging eight. The WR3 of the Giants, Darnell Mooney, left with a neck injury in Week 6, and if he is sidelined at all, Fields should continue to at least see a more increased role than the one he had in his first five games of 2026.

Also helping Fields' chances of being a possible fantasy starting option in 2026 is the usage of New York's passing attack of late. In the Giants' past three games, they are averaging the second-most passing yards per game in the NFL, 304.7. Fields in ESPN fantasy leagues is rostered by 5.4% of teams.

TE2 on his own team, so what. While the Las Vegas Raiders have one of their best TEs in the NFL, Brock Bowers, as the season has gone on, their TE2, Michael Mayer, has continually generated notable fantasy points. In Week 6 against the Buffalo Bills, he had seven receptions on nine targets for 95 yards. His sample size of having games like these is starting to get too big to ignore. Overall, through six weeks, he ranks as TE10 in PPR formats in fantasy, ahead of a couple of highly regarded fantasy TEs. Bills TE Dalton Kincaid and Green Bay Packers TE Tucker Kraft.

Despite his production, he is available on most waiver wires, and his production looks like it could be sustainable. The lowest snap share he has had in a week was 65%, and he has played in over 80% of snaps in four of six games. In ESPN fantasy leagues, he is currently rostered by 14.9% of teams.

Yes, his tenure with the Minnesota Vikings was a disaster, but in his second stint with the Giants, J.J. McCarthy looked great. Against the New Orleans Saints, he went 11-of-21 for 243 passing yards and had a 1-1 TD-to-INT ratio. He is expected to be named the Giants' starter at QB ahead of veteran Jameis Winston going into Week 7.

With the volume that the Giants have thrown the ball of late, McCarthy could possibly be a must-start in certain matchups moving forward this season. He is currently rostered by 0.9% of teams in ESPN fantasy leagues.

articles.title: 49ers-Commanders preview: A George Kittle breakout game is in the cards
articles.summary: A deep dive into tonight’s matchup between the 49ers and Commanders
articles.body:
Recent history will point you in the correct direction if you're wondering how certain NFL games will go. For example, the Washington Commanders are coming off a game they should have won against a divisional foe. Those contests can take an emotional toll.

Since 2022, Washington has won only once the week after playing the New York Giants. Six of those losses were by at least a touchdown.

Conversely, the 49ers have won eight of their previous nine games against the NFC East, with the one loss carrying the biggest asterisk, the 2022 NFC Championship Game. The Niners have dominated the division, even when they were undermanned.

It's hard to envision something changing in the final game of Week 6. The Commanders are allowing 29.8 points per game, a point less than what the 49ers are scoring. Let's get into the preview: we expect the Commanders to land a few punches, but the Niners' haymakers to overcome Washington.

The 49ers' surprisingly stout run defense

The Commanders rank 12th in EPA per rush and 19th in rushing success rate this season. They rank middle of the pack in yards after contact but fourth in yards before contact per attempt, a sign their scheme is sound.

They'll be without their leading rusher, Bill Croskey-Merritt. He has double the carries of any running back on the roster. The only other player with a double-digit run this season is Rachaad White. White last rushed for over 70 yards in December 2024. Even with Croskey-Merritt, the running backs have a 37.6% success rate and average -0.159 EPA per carry.

Jayden Daniels' legs uplift a pedestrian rushing attack. Daniels ran for 103 yards against the Giants last week and 69 yards against Dallas in Week 2. The objective will be to rush Daniels with integrity and keep him in the pocket .

The 49ers have allowed the second-fewest scramble yards in the NFL. They also run zone coverage 83% of the time, the fourth-highest clip in the league. Dallas and Washington are top-10 in man coverage usage, which explains Daniels' success on the ground.

Daniels is an excellent runner. He has the second-most scramble yards this season and is averaging an incredible 12.6 yards per carry on those runs. He has generated nine explosive runs, tied with Josh Allen for the most in the league.

However, the Niners have faced only five scrambles, the fewest in the league. They are limiting quarterbacks to 5.6 yards per carry, the sixth-lowest mark. They did keep Malik Willis in check against Miami.

The Niners lead the NFL in explosive rush rate and rush rate over expectation. It's not in their DNA to allow the big play.

The biggest surprise for the 49ers this season is their run defense. They boast a 41.5% rushing success rate, five percentage points better than their first five games a season ago. That's also good enough for sixth in the NFL. The Niners are also sixth in EPA per rush. Whether it's on a down-to-down basis or limiting explosive plays, Raheem Morris's scheme is getting the job done.

Morris's 5-down fronts take away the B-gap bubble and keep Fred Warner clean. As you can see from the picture below, Morris has consistently put two defenders on one guard — in this case, the right guard — which has led to chaos in the backfield:

Jaden Dugger gets the spot start with Dre Greenlaw suspended . Dugger was relentless against the Seahawks last week. If that aggression and discipline carry over into Monday night, Washington could abandon the run entirely.

San Francisco should make Washington one-dimensional. But is that a good thing?

49ers X-factor: Mykel Williams played 22 snaps in his first game back. Seattle averaged 3.18 yards per play with Williams on the field. Williams' edge-setting prowess will be needed against a Commanders offense that runs outside zone at the third-highest percentage in the NFL.

Kyle Shanahan spoke glowingly about Daniels last week:

"Since he came in the league until now, Jayden's got a chance to be one of the better quarterbacks in this league without a doubt. If you take away the running element of him, just how he plays in the pocket is so natural with how accurate he is, how strong his arm is, how poised he is going through a progression, how fearless he is hanging in there and taking a hit, keeping his eyes down the field. When you take that out, how scary he is just running the ball. He's got the speed and the coordination to win games only with his legs, which means you want to keep him in the pocket and not let him out because he can beat you with his legs. However, he's a very scary quarterback in the pocket just playing the position. So, he's got all the tools to be as good as there is."

Daniels is everything you want in a quarterback when you take him No. 1 overall. He's unquestionably the most talented quarterback the Niners will have faced this season.

Daniels has generated more EPA than Matthew Stafford despite playing 235 fewer snaps. He's one of the league's most aggressive quarterbacks. Daniels is throwing deep on nearly 16% of his passes, the third-highest mark in the NFL. The 49ers secondary will be tested in ways it hasn't been against Daniels.

Daniels has the arm talent to throw the ball on a line over the intermediate portion of the field and zip it in between linebackers, or loft it 30 yards downfield and drop it into a bucket. He can make all those throws and is willing to sacrifice his body to take a big hit.

The combination of those traits is what makes Daniels an enigma. I'm more inclined to believe Washington's shortcomings are more about Daniels' surroundings than the quarterback himself.

When he is in the lineup, his go-to targets have been Antonio Williams, Terry McLaurin, and Stefon Diggs, who missed Week 5 with a hamstring injury but practiced on Friday.

McLaurin runs 77.3% of his routes on the outside and has caught only 53.8% of his targets. With the way Morris has structured his defense, the McLaurins of the world are rarely targeted. He's the kind of wideout who Deommodore Lenoir should match up well against.

Diggs has the highest target share of the trio. He has 15 targets in two games with Daniels for nine receptions and three touchdowns. He moves around the formation the most, with 39% of his routes coming outside compared to 59% in the slot. You'd like to see the Niners be aggressive with Diggs and sit on his routes, especially with a hamstring injury.

Commanders X-factor: The rookie is who could give the Niners the most fits. He's speedy and the kind of wideout who runs away from coverage. Williams' best game came against Vic Fangio in Week 1, where he had a 33-yarder. Williams against Upton Stout or the safeties could be an advantage for Washington. It feels like a game where Daniels forces the Niners' nickel/safeties to cover.

The Commanders may hit an explosive with McLaurin or Williams. But the Niners have the fifth-best passing success rate. Limiting the body blows and keeping Washington in longer down-and-distance situations should win out in the end.

The Niners are content with letting offenses dink and dunk their way down the field. No defense allows more targets and receiving yards to running backs. If it's a game where Rachaad White has 6 receptions for 60 yards, then so be it. It beats the alternative of McLaurin or Williams beating you over the top.

Daniels has been pressured on over 45% of his dropbacks. Washington has used a couple of different lineups with Nick Allegretti rotating between center and right guard. Keion White, Osa Odighizuwa, and Gracen Halton can disrupt the interior and go a long way toward getting the Commanders off the field.

It's easy to wonder why Christian McCaffrey wasn't involved in hindsight after Week 5, especially given how successful the plays were when he ran the ball. But Kyle Shanahan faced Seattle three times a year ago, and his offensive line got pushed around and gave McCaffrey little to no yards.

The Commanders are league average in EPA per rush allowed, but 27th in rushing success rate. With an extra day, McCaffrey should be fresh. They've been stingy at defending outsize zone.

Washington has allowed 2.81 yards per carry, with a -0.39 EPA per rush and a 36.1% success rate. Outside zone is still the 49ers' predominant run (40%), but they've incorporated inside zone more than ever (20% of the time) and man concepts to keep defenses off balance.

Those inside runs will come in handy against a Commanders defense that has allowed six, yes, six yards per carry against inside zone. They've also allowed an EPA per rush of +0.115 on man concepts. So, plenty of McCaffrey with a sprinkle of Kaelon Black should keep the Niners in manageable passing situations for their quarterback, who can expect a blitz-heavy evening .

49ers X-factor: People are also forgetting that the recipe that has ignited the running game this year was missing a key ingredient. Kyle Juszczyk is expected to return, which means the running game should.

ESPN's Adam Schefter said, "My guess is we will see Mike Evans tonight" on the Pat McAfee show. The 49ers will see how Evans looks pre-game, but there is optimism he'll play. How much Evans is involved in the offense is a different discussion. He already had a rib injury, and Achilles soreness popped up late last week.

Evans is coming off a season-high 113 yards. It's a favorable matchup, as Washington is 29th in the NFL at allowing receiving yards and targets to wide receivers. But with a short week coming up, you'd think Evans wouldn't be heavily involved.

So where will Brock Purdy look to against a defense that blitzes 45% of the time? Let's clear some things up here. The Commanders blitzing basically every other down shouldn't be conflated with their ability to bring down the quarterback—Washington's sack percentage is 25th this year. Purdy has been tremendous at maneuvering in the pocket and running out of sacks all season.

They are 26th in passing success rate allowed and 23rd in EPA per pass. Last week, the 49ers planted seeds for an offense that could center on George Kittle. I think we see that come to fruition on Monday night.

No team allows more touchdowns to tight ends than Washington. They also allow the most red zone touchdowns to the position. Isaiah Likely caught 11 of 13 targets last week. Washington ranks in the bottom three in receptions, targets, and pass rate over expectation against tight ends. Funneling targets to the middle of the field against a Kyle Shanahan offense is problematic, to say the least. It's especially bad when you're allowing the sixth-most yards after the catch to tight ends.

After a low-usage game against Seattle, paired with the injury to Evans and the other injuries at the position, Week 6 has the makings of a classic Kittle game in primetime.

If you're worried about Purdy holding up against the blitz, fret not. He's completed 28 of his 40 attempts for 10.9 yards per attempt. He has eight touchdowns compared to one interception. Purdy knows the offense inside and out, and has a knack for replacing the blitzer and hunting big plays. He fights pressure with pressure, and that's one of his many MVP traits.

Washington has depth along the defensive line and a handful of players with double-digit pressure percentages, but this game should prove sacks are the ultimate measure, because you can still complete a pass if you're pressured.

The offense left yards on the table last week. Washington gives up the most second-half points in the NFL. Shanahan should keep his foot on the gas all game. This game could be one where San Francisco takes it out on their opponent and where they lack after a poor offensive showing a week ago.

Commanders X-factor: Rookie Sonny Styles will be in the middle of the action tonight, given how the Niners operate. They'll run right at him, use eye candy to get Styles out of position in coverage, and prey on the rookie who faces his toughest test and matchup to date.

Jayden Daniels makes everybody rethink their stance on the 49ers, despite playing without Nick Bosa and Dre Greenlaw. The secondary gets a reality check when the pass rush can't bail them out, and the Commanders capitalize in the red zone.

But it isn't enough to slow Purdy and Kittle as the offense marches up and down the field all night and does what it's done in every fourth quarter: go for the kill shot.

articles.title: Nick Saban recalls kind gesture from Jalen Hurts amid ex-Alabama football QB health concerns
articles.summary: Nick Saban will remember his former Alabama football QB Jalen Hurts as a "first class guy." How Saban is showing support amid Hurts' health scare.
articles.body:
BIRMINGHAM — Nick Saban has yet to hear from Jalen Hurts since news of health concerns have put the future of his NFL season with the Philadelphia Eagles on hold. He is keeping one of his former Alabama football quarterbacks in mind, though.

Before speaking to the Monday Morning Quarterback Club at the Harbert Center on Monday, Oct. 19, Saban said he had texted Hurts. He also shared that the Super Bowl champ sent the "prettiest flowers" to Saban and wife Miss Terry following the release of the Saban docuseries on ESPN.

"He's such a first-class guy," Saban said.

Updates on Hurts' health have grown since Thursday, Oct. 15, when it was revealed that Hurts would miss a Week 6 matchup with the Carolina Panthers after being diagnosed with a blood clot, which was found in a follow-up ultrasound for a calf injury.

Nick Saban's 'thoughts and prayers' with Jalen Hurts amid health concerns

By Saturday, Oct. 17, Hurts was placed on injured reserve. The following Monday, the Eagles announced that Hurts was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli and multiple reports surfaced that the blood clot moved to Hurts' lungs. Ian Rapoport reported that Hurts will miss the rest of the year with the ailment.

"We thanked him for all the support, told him our thoughts and prayers are with him for a speedy recovery, so I'm sure I'll hear from him," Saban said.

Emilee Smarr covers Alabama basketball and Crimson Tide athletics for The Tuscaloosa News. She can be reached via email at esmarr@usatodayco.com.

articles.title: Mike Evans' comments about 49ers raise questions for Buccaneers
articles.summary: Mike Evans explains why he left the Buccaneers for the 49ers, praising San Francisco's win-now approach as Tampa Bay struggles through a 1-5 start.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have struggled to find answers during their 1-5 start, while one of the franchise's most recognizable players is enjoying a fresh start elsewhere. After spending 12 seasons in Tampa Bay, Mike Evans is opening up about his decision to join the San Francisco 49ers, and his explanation comes at an interesting time for his former team.

According to Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times , Evans discussed what attracted him to San Francisco and how the move has affected his outlook on the remainder of his NFL career.

"This team rejuvenated me and probably added a few more years to my career," Evans said.

Evans went on to explain that San Francisco offered the situation he was looking for at this stage of his career. He pointed to the quarterback, offensive playmakers, defense, coaching staff, and organization while emphasizing the 49ers' commitment to competing for a championship.

Those comments weren't a direct criticism of Tampa Bay, but they do raise questions about what Evans believed San Francisco could offer him that he wasn't finding elsewhere. After spending more than a decade with the Buccaneers, winning a Super Bowl and establishing himself as one of the greatest players in franchise history, Evans chose to continue his career with another organization.

The contrast between the two teams is difficult to ignore: San Francisco entered Week 6 with a 5-0 record, while Tampa Bay dropped to 1-5 after Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Buccaneers held a 13-point lead entering the fourth quarter before Pittsburgh came back to win in overtime, exposing many of the same offensive inconsistencies that have troubled them throughout the season.

Meanwhile, Evans has continued producing wins with the 49ers. Through five games, the veteran receiver has recorded 24 receptions for 326 yards and three touchdowns, providing San Francisco with another experienced weapon in its passing attack.

For Tampa Bay, the concern isn't simply that Evans is finding success elsewhere. The Buccaneers still have receiving talent in Chris Godwin, Emeka Egbuka, and their younger players, but the offense has struggled to consistently put those weapons in positions to succeed. Against Pittsburgh, Jalon Daniels attempted 43 passes for just 164 yards, and Tampa Bay finished with only 224 total yards.

Evans never specifically said that the Buccaneers lacked the qualities he praised in San Francisco. Still, hearing a longtime franchise cornerstone emphasize winning, coaching, and organizational direction while his former team struggles through a disappointing season naturally invites questions about where Tampa Bay stands.

Evans gave the Buccaneers 12 seasons of production and helped deliver a championship. His decision to leave doesn't erase any of that. However, his comments offer a glimpse into what mattered most as he entered the next chapter of his career, and the Buccaneers' current struggles make that decision difficult to overlook.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni backs Sean Mannion as Eagles’ offensive struggles continue
articles.summary: Nick Sirianni expressed confidence in Sean Mannion and confirmed he remains the Eagles’ play-caller after Philadelphia’s fourth straight loss
articles.body:
Sean Mannion remains the Eagles' offensive play-caller, and Nick Sirianni expressed confidence in him Monday while acknowledging Philadelphia needs better results.

When asked directly whether Mannion was still calling plays, Sirianni said, "Yes." According to The Philadelphia Inquirer's Jeff McLane, Sirianni said he has confidence in all his coaches, including Mannion, and will spend the next few days identifying ways to improve the offense. The endorsement follows a 25-14 loss to Carolina that extended Philadelphia's losing streak to four games and dropped the Eagles to 2-4. With Tanner McKee starting at quarterback, Philadelphia generated 222 total yards, rushed for just 35 yards and punted eight times. McKee completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards and a touchdown without an interception, but the Eagles averaged only 4.8 yards per attempt. Three sacks cost another 28 yards, while 11 penalties for 84 yards compounded the execution problems.

There were productive stretches. DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert combined for 13 catches and 136 yards, and Smith's fourth-quarter touchdown cut the lead to 19-14. However, the next offensive possession unraveled with a bad snap, and an eight-yard deflected punt helped set up Carolina's final touchdown.

Mannion now faces the challenge of building a more consistent offense without Jalen Hurts, who is out for the season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Injuries elsewhere have further complicated the task, particularly in the backfield.

Sirianni's response establishes continuity in play-calling responsibilities as the team prepares for Dallas. The pressure remains on Mannion and the entire offensive staff to turn that backing into sustained drives, fewer mistakes, and enough production to stop Philadelphia's slide.

articles.title: Texans WR Tank Dell to return from gruesome 2024 knee injury on Sunday vs. Giants
articles.summary: Tank Dell missed all of last season recovering from a knee injury he suffered late in 2024.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024.

"I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there," Ryans said, via ESPN Radio's Will Kunkel . "He is as quick as ever."

"I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there," Ryans said, via ESPN Radio's Will Kunkel .

Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome.

He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day.

Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments , sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since.

The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally.

Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston.

Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. After losing four straight to start the year, they've now won back-to-back contests entering Sunday's matchup with the Giants at NRG Stadium. They most recently rallied to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy, Jameis Winston Giants QB1 Competition Discussed by John Harbaugh Ahead of Texans Game
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy played well in place of Jameis Winston during Sunday's loss to the New Orleans Saints, but New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh isn't ready to announce the starting quarterback for the upcoming game against the Houston Texans just yet.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy played well in place of Jameis Winston during Sunday's loss to the New Orleans Saints, but New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh isn't ready to announce the starting quarterback for the upcoming game against the Houston Texans just yet.

"We're working through that now. Honing in on a decision," he told reporters Monday while saying a determination of "what gives us the best chance to win the football game" will be considered.

The quarterback position has been a roller coaster this season for the Giants.

Presumed franchise signal-caller Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury, which forced Winston into action. The Florida State product started poorly with zero touchdown passes and an interception against the Los Angeles Rams and Tennessee Titans but then directed a win over the Arizona Cardinals with three touchdown passes to two interceptions.

He then led the Giants' comeback in a 27-27 tie to the Washington Commanders with three touchdown passes to zero interceptions and seemed to be the quarterback the team would rely on for the rest of the season even though it traded for McCarthy shortly after Dart's injury.

However, things may have changed Sunday.

Winston struggled with two interceptions as New York fell behind 34-10 in the fourth quarter and decided to give McCarthy a chance. And it didn't get much better in the immediate aftermath, as the Michigan product threw an interception on his first possession.

However, he led three scoring drives with two touchdowns and a field goal in the fourth quarter and drove all the way to the Saints' 14-yard line with a chance to tie it in the final seconds before turning it over on downs.

It was a valiant comeback effort, and McCarthy finished 11-of-21 for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

While he never lived up to expectations with the Minnesota Vikings as the No. 10 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft, McCarthy may have a chance to build on Sunday's showing and turn things around with the Giants depending on Harbaugh's decision.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Blasted by Rival NFL Coach, 'No One Feels Good' About Seahawks QB in 2-Minute Drill
articles.summary: Sam Darnold threw a pair of interceptions late in Thursday's 17-14 loss against the Denver Broncos, ultimately costing his team a chance to win the game.
articles.body:
Sam Darnold threw a pair of interceptions late in Thursday's 17-14 loss against the Denver Broncos, ultimately costing his team a chance to win the game.

They were his sixth and seventh interceptions of the season through four full starts, a concerning trend. Certainly eyebrows are raising around the NFL.

"They are 3-3, and they probably have a 3-3 quarterback," a defensive coach from another team told The Athletic's Mike Sando . "No one feels good with Sam Darnold having to play two-minute (offense) to win, right? Not Kevin O'Connell, not Mike Macdonald, not any of his other coaches who had him felt good about it."

Darnold, 29, led the team to a Super Bowl title last season and has generally been a different player since a 2023 season with Mike Shanahan in San Francisco then he was early in his career, when he struggled mightily with the New York Jets and Carolina Panthers. But it's clear that the turnover-happy player of his youth is still lurking under the surface at times.

In 2024, for example, Darnold led the Minnesota Vikings to a 14-3 record and a playoff berth, but was awful in the Wild Card Round, throwing a pick and taking nine sacks in a 27-9 loss against the Los Angeles Rams. He also threw four picks against the Rams during a regular-season loss in 2025.

In general, Darnold has been a great addition for the Seahawks, given last year's title. But his 2026 season has gotten off to a worrying start.

articles.title: Everything Nick Sirianni Said on Jalen Hurts Playing for Eagles, Flying After Blood Clot Diagnosis
articles.summary: With Jalen Hurts potentially sidelined for the season with blood clots and reports circulating about how the situation was handled for the team's Week 5 trip to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars, Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni addressed the media Monday.
articles.body:
With Jalen Hurts potentially sidelined for the season with blood clots and reports circulating about how the situation was handled for the team's Week 5 trip to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars, Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni addressed the media Monday.

"The health of our players is always at the forefront of our mind," he said in his initial comments. "We'll leave that up to the medical experts. But we always, always care deeply about our players."

He was then asked about Hurts playing in the game and said (three-minute mark), "I'm not a medical expert. I lean on those guys in all those situations. I'm a football coach, I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them. It's not just me that has major care for our players, it's them as well."

Sirianni was then asked why Hurts flew home after the game, and he reiterated that he is not a medical expert and "always put the players' health first and foremost in every situation."

He also continued to point to the team's statement that was released Monday that said, in part, "He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. … Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery.

"We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."

Sirianni's press conference came after Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported Monday that Hurts is expected to miss the season "after new imaging over the weekend found several blood clots in his lungs."

Notably Pelissero also reported Hurts was told not to sleep after he was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London, which meant he was awake for "roughly 36 hours when he started against the Jaguars."

However, Pelissero followed up and said he spoke to Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, who said the quarterback was able to sleep at the stadium after rejoining the team following an evaluation at the hospital.

Lynn also released a statement on the situation:

Philadelphia ended up losing that game 19-17 after Ameer Abdullah's long kickoff return set up Cam Little's game-winning 57-yard field goal in the final seconds. Hurts went 21-of-40 for 220 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions.

He was sidelined for the following game against the Carolina Panthers, which was a 25-14 loss for the Eagles.

Tanner McKee played in his place and will presumably remain under center when Philadelphia takes on the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer Hot-Seat Buzz Addressed by Cowboys' Stephen Jones After Packers Loss
articles.summary: Despite a 2-4 start to the season for the Dallas Cowboys, head coach Brian Schottenheimer's job is not in jeopardy.
articles.body:
Despite a 2-4 start to the season for the Dallas Cowboys, head coach Brian Schottenheimer's job is not in jeopardy.

The team's executive vice president, Stephen Jones, said Schottenheimer "has the team."

"There's not any question in (Cowboys owner Jerry Jones') and my mind," he said on 105.3 The Fan (h/t The Athletic's Jon Machota ). "He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen. Feel really good about our coaching staff. We just got to have it continue to evolve and get to a point to where we can win these football games."

Jones' comments come after Dallas' 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers, a game Jones called "very disappointing." Still, Jones is confident the Cowboys can turn things around.

"But at the same time, we got a lot of football to play," Jones said. "We've got resolve. We just got to go back to work. We like the players. We like the coaches."

Much like last year, Dallas' offense has been mostly competent while the defense has lacked. That wasn't the case Sunday, though, when both units struggled.

The Cowboys at least need the offensive trio of Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to do their job. From there, it's a matter of getting the defense to click.

But even after the rough start, it appears Schottenheimer has some breathing room in his second season. If things continue to get worse, Jones' tone may change at the end of the season.

articles.title: Braylon Edwards Trolls 'Mid' Cowboys HC Schottenheimer, Reflects on Jets' 'Terrible' AFC Title Runs
articles.summary: Former NFL wide receiver Braylon Edwards thinks he knows what the problem is for the 2-4 Dallas Cowboys this season.
articles.body:
Former NFL wide receiver Braylon Edwards thinks he knows what the problem is for the 2-4 Dallas Cowboys this season.

Edwards took to social media Monday and said "mid" Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who was also the offensive coordinator for his 2009 and 2010 New York Jets that reached the AFC Championship Game in back-to-back seasons, seems to be the issue:

While Schottenheimer has an offensive background, Dallas is a solid-but-unspectacular 13th in the league in yards this season and 11th in scoring despite having weapons that include Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Javonte Williams.

The numbers are notably similar to the 2010 Jets that finished 11th in yards and 13th in points after they were 20th in yards and 17th in points the previous year.

Edwards doesn't seem to be a big fan of Schottenheimer's work, but the No. 3 overall pick of the 2005 NFL draft who made just one Pro Bowl in his eight years in the league enjoyed the second-best season of his career in 2010 in the coach's offense.

He finished with 904 receiving yards and seven touchdown catches, which were his second-best numbers in each category behind his one Pro Bowl year in 2007.

As for this year's Cowboys, the offense is going to have to be better if they are going to be realistic contenders in the NFC. After all, the defense is 30th in yards allowed and 25th in points allowed and was not expected to be a dominant unit this season.

The offense, on the other hand, was expected to carry the team with so many playmakers on that side of the ball.

That offense managed just 13 points in Sunday's 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers with the final touchdown coming after the game was well in hand in the final minute. It wasn't good enough to compete against an NFC contender and will need to take strides if there is going to be meaningful improvement.

And it will be up to Schottenheimer to figure out how to unlock better production.

articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams' already-disappointing 2026 season took another rough turn on Monday.

The Los Angeles Rams' already-disappointing 2026 season took another rough turn on Monday.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the star wideout will be sidelined for 6-10 weeks due to a ruptured hamstring suffered in Sunday's 18-16 loss against the Arizona Cardinals.

The Rams, who came into the season as Super Bowl contenders but have limped to a 2-4 start, are now beset by injuries.

Superstar edge-rusher Myles Garrett was already on injured reserve, star cornerback Trent McDuffie missed Sunday's game with a groin issue and Monday's injury report hit hard beyond just Adams:

The 33-year-old was having an excellent season, catching 30 passes for 480 yards and four scores while giving the Rams one of the most dynamic wideout duos in the league alongside Puka Nacua.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud Is a QB 'That Can F--king Deal It with Anybody,' Says Schultz After Texans' Win vs. Jags
articles.summary: The Houston Texans' offense was plenty confident that C.J. Stroud could lead the team to a game-winning score when they took over with 1:49 remaining in the fourth quarter during Sunday's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans' offense was plenty confident that C.J. Stroud could lead the team to a game-winning score when they took over with 1:49 remaining in the fourth quarter during Sunday's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

"It was, 'S--t, we're in business,'" tight end Dalton Schultz told The Athletic's Michael Silver . "You give us a bunch of timeouts and two minutes on the clock, and we have a quarterback that can f--king deal it with anybody. He's dealing it as good as anybody in the league."

The confidence was founded. Stroud drove the Texans 36 yards in six plays, setting up Ka'imi Fairbairn's game-winning, 49-yard field goal in the 34-31 victory.

Stroud, much besieged after disappointing seasons in 2024 and 2025, has thrown for 1,714 yards, nine touchdowns and just one interception this season. He looks far more like the player who took the league by storm as a rookie, and in the process has led the Texans to a pair of wins after a rough 0-4 start.

"His back's against the wall. Like, he obviously felt some type of way after last year and came in with a f--king laser-locked focus, and I think it's just allowed him to elevate his game to a whole new level," Schultz noted.

articles.title: Saleh Reacts to Cam Ward, Titans' Upset Win vs. Colts After Being 'Punching Bag of' NFL
articles.summary: It would have been easy for the Tennessee Titans to fold and go through the motions for the rest of the season after a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans dropped their record to 0-5, but they did the opposite and responded with a 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.
articles.body:
It would have been easy for the Tennessee Titans to fold and go through the motions for the rest of the season after a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans dropped their record to 0-5, but they did the opposite and responded with a 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.

Head coach Robert Saleh reflected on the effort that took.

"This was our hardest week of practice," he said, per Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated . "Not necessarily because of the work we put in but because it's hard when you're 0–5 and you just got punched in the mouth by a division opponent after what you felt was progress. And you're the punching bag of the entire league. And that, to me, is where everyone can say, 'I'm done.'

"And it was a hard week. There was a lot of truth told. There was a lot of discussions had, and the resilience of the group to stand up, wake up this morning and make the decision to go win a football game, make the plays and accept the challenges that were made, we got the right guys in this group. We got the right guys in this locker room. They're all made of the right stuff."

There was resilience within the game, as the Titans overcame a 13-3 deficit in the second half.

Carnell Tate started the comeback with a fourth-quarter touchdown catch before the Tennessee special teams gave the visitors the lead with a touchdown on a punt block. While the Colts tied it with fewer than six minutes remaining, the Titans added two field goals down the stretch to leave with the win.

It was the franchise's first win since Dec. 21 of last year, but Saleh believes things are going to turn around in the future.

"This organization is going to have its day in the sun," he said. "We're going to win a lot of football games here. And typically when you're trying to rebuild something, you're always going to run into one of these weeks. And I thought our guys passed the test with flying colors."

This is Saleh's first season as the head coach of the Titans after previous stops as the head coach of the New York Jets and defensive coordinator of the San Francisco 49ers.

Despite the victory, it will likely take some time for the Titans to start contending for playoff spots as they focus on a rebuild in the immediate future. But Sunday's outcome seemed like an important step in that process and drew praise from the head coach.

articles.title: Rams WR Davante Adams will miss 6-10 weeks with ruptured hamstring, Sean McVay says
articles.summary: Adams appeared to injure himself on the final drive of Sunday's loss to the Cardinals.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without star wide receiver Davante Adams for quite some time.

In a press conference Monday, Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Adams ruptured his hamstring. He will be out six to 10 weeks with the injury.

Adams appeared to injure himself on the final drive of Sunday's loss to the Arizona Cardinals. The 33-year-old receiver pulled up suddenly and started hopping in the back of the end zone before limping off the field. The Cardinals won the game with a late rally and a walk-off field goal.

Adams leads the Rams in receiving yards this season and was a key part of the team's offense with players like Puka Nacua missing time at the start of the year. In six games, Adams had racked up 480 receiving yards and four touchdowns.

A six-week recovery would see Adams returning to the field in December, while 10 could mean the receiver would be back in time for the last two regular-season games in January. Given the timeline, the Rams will likely place Adams on injured reserve.

Adams is one of four significant injuries McVay announced Monday: Defensive tackle Poona Ford is out for the year with a tricep injury, while DT Kobie Turner is headed to injured reserve with a groin injury. Kicker Blake Grupe, who just signed with the team last week, is also out for the season with a knee injury after he attempted a tackle early in Sunday's game.

The loss to Arizona dropped the Rams to 2-4, a stunning turn of events for a team that was heavily touted ahead of the regular season.

articles.summary: CJ Gardiner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct and has been suspended for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players in their nail-biting 33-30 win at Allegiant Stadium
articles.body:
Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers.

In issuing the suspension, the NFL cited its rule applying to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship".

With Buffalo (5-1) entering their bye week, Gardiner-Johnson's suspension will begin on October 26 and run through November 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens.

The player has the right to appeal the suspension.

Gardner-Johnson apologised to his team-mates immediately following Buffalo's 33-30 win and posted a note on social media apologising to fans.

"I owe my team-mates an apology and to be a man about it," Gardner-Johnson said following the game.

"You got to understand that as a grown man you can't be doing [stuff] like that in a game," he added. "As a vet, I'll be better. I'll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on."

The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons, and signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March.

Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson's spitting act as being "inexcusable" and said he discussed the matter privately with the player.

"It can't happen. That's not what we're about. That's not what the game of football is about, and he knows that," Brady said.

Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits.

"I don't need a roster of everybody being the same person," Brady said.

"Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can't happen. It won't happen again. Personality-wise, I'm not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do."

Tom Brady is still relatively new to the broadcasting world, but some think he's already the best analyst in the game.

"I would not have said that two years ago or last year, but Brady is (clearly) the best," an NFL team exec said, per The Athletic's Mike Sando . "He is critical. He has gotten better. He is punchy."

Those comments come amid what could be a pivotal offseason for top analysts and broadcasters.

ESPN's Troy Aikman is set to be a free agent at the end of the season, and there reportedly is "tension" between him and his partner, Joe Buck, over Aikman's lack of a new contract.

Greg Olsen, who was relegated to Fox's No. 2 booth after Brady joined the team, will be a free agent after this season as well and is sure to command a high price tag.

Former Philadelphia Eagles star Jason Kelce has joined ESPN and could be in line for an analyst gig, as could Pat McAfee, one of ESPN's biggest names.

Top analysts earn more than many NFL players and coaches, which begs the question of whether more coaches will leave the sideline for the booth. Sando noted Sean McVay as a potential candidate to do just that.

"I don't know how many people wanted to do the job when it was not paying as much," an NFL coach said, per Sando. "They are all going to make more money than they are making on the field, including McVay. We'll see at the end of the year what (Mike) Tomlin wants to do, but my belief is, the money is too good."

Still, the glory of being a winning coach might outweigh the check that comes with being an analyst.

"The money is crazy, but they will all ultimately want to chase the competition," a team exec said, per Sando. "The only thing better than talking about the guy on the podium is being the guy on the podium."
