articles.title: Rams Announce Roster Move Involving Injured Kicker After Week 6 Loss
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams will be looking for another kicker after announcing their latest roster move. The post Rams Announce Roster Move Involving Injured Kicke...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are officially in panic mode after suffering an ugly 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6. With a 2-4 record, the presumed Super Bowl favorite entering the season is trending in the wrong direction, and it's becoming abundantly clear that changes need to be made.

Entering this game, the Rams were rolling with a new kicker, Blake Grupe, after Harrison Mevis was released in the wake of their overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 5. Grupe didn't even make it through a quarter of action with L.A. before he was forced out of the game with a knee injury, which prompted L.A. to make a roster move involving him.

Rams Place Blake Grupe on Injured Reserve

Special teams has been a longstanding issue for Los Angeles, and that has stood true to begin the 2026 campaign. Mevis took over as the Rams' kicker midway through last season, but after hitting just five of his nine field goal attempts through his first five games this season (which included a pair of misses against the Bills), the team opted to move on from him.

Mevis' replacement ended up being Grupe, who had spent the beginning of the season on the New York Jets practice squad. Early on against the Cardinals , Grupe seemed to indicate that he was a significant upgrade over Mevis, as he easily converted a 44-yard field goal on his first kick for his new team.

On the ensuing kickoff, though, Grupe badly hurt himself when attempting to tackle Devin Duvernay , and he was quickly ruled out of the game with a knee injury, forcing Los Angeles to get through the rest of the game without a kicker. It looks like the team will have to find a new kicker for the second straight week, as Grupe was placed on injured reserve Monday afternoon.

LA Rams Transactions: Reserve/Injured K Blake Grupe ," the team announced in a post on X.

Rams Must Immediately Find a Replacement for Blake Grupe

It's been a comedy of errors for L.A. when it comes to special teams, but unlike in years past, its issues go beyond just this unit. The offense cannot consistently string together scoring drives, and the defense hasn't been the sort of game-changing unit everyone was expecting it to be. Put everything together, and you have one of the most disappointing teams in the entire league through the first six weeks of action.

While the San Francisco 49ers are running away with the NFC West division in the early going, the Rams have way too much talent to be ruled out of the running for a playoff spot just yet. They have a lot of work to do, though, and it starts with finding a new kicker, as Grupe will miss four games at the very least. Los Angeles will be back in action in Week 7 for what will be a tougher-than-expected matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders .

articles.title: Bryce Young Hyped as '1-of-1 Player' by Chuba Hubbard After Panthers Beat Eagles amid Contract Buzz
articles.summary: Bryce Young had a rocky start to his NFL career, but has started to show that he's capable of being the Carolina Panthers' franchise quarterback.
articles.body:
Bryce Young had a rocky start to his NFL career, but has started to show that he's capable of being the Carolina Panthers' franchise quarterback.

After another strong performance from Young in a win over the Philadelphia Eagles, Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard had high praise for him.

"He's a one-of-one guy. He's a one-of-one player. Each year, he's just gotten better," Hubbard told Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer . "But I've said it since Day 1, been in his corner, he's a special type of guy. He can make plays that not everyone can make. … And he's cool, calm, collected in all moments. So it brings confidence to the offense and we're lucky to have him."

Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns in the 25-14 win, which put the Panthers at 3-2 on the season.

The former No. 1 overall pick is up to 1,549 yards, 11 touchdowns and just two interceptions this year. He's coming off a career season that saw him collect 3,011 yards and 23 touchdowns, and he's on pace to shatter his previous career highs.

articles.title: Rams' mounting injuries could strip playoff stakes from Seahawks games
articles.summary: The NFL expected this rivalry to be as anticipated as any in 2026. At this point, though, one or both teams could be out of the playoff race entirely.
articles.body:
While the Seattle Seahawks have faced their fair share of trials and tribulations thus far in 2026, even they can't hold a candle to the injury problem plaguing their NFC West rival Los Angeles Rams . On Monday afternoon, Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters that star wide receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 and will miss 6-10 weeks.

McVay also confirmed that starting defensive tackles Poona Ford and Kobie Turner will miss extended time , and that newly signed kicker Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL in that game and will miss the rest of the season. It doesn't end there — McVay also mentioned that defensive end Myles Garrett will not return to practice this week, and cornerback Trent McDuffie is "progressing but uncertain" for Week 7.

After being eliminated from the playoffs by the eventual NFC champion in back-to-back seasons, the Rams went all-in on contending in 2026. They gave up a haul, including their 2027 first-round draft pick, to acquire reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Garrett from the Cleveland Browns . They traded their 2026 first-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for McDuffie to round out their defense. Without either of them available, they've sunk to the bottom of the division and are currently just 2-4.

While the Seahawks' worries are warranted — they're disappointed in a 3-3 start and look as beatable as they did at any point last year — they just need to look at the Rams to remind themselves: It could always be worse. They have all their draft picks and expect to return reinforcements to their running back room in the coming weeks in the form of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

The NFL scheduled these two teams in Weeks 16 and 18, expecting those games to be as anticipated as any this season. At this point, though, one or both teams could be out of the playoff race entirely.

articles.title: Why did Dre Greenlaw get suspended by the NFL for Monday night's game?
articles.summary: Here's why we won't see Dre Greenlaw suit up for the 49ers on Monday night.
articles.body:
The undefeated San Francisco 49ers have weathered the storm well heading into their Monday night tilt with the Washington Commanders . But sometimes, things can be out of an organization's control. That's why we won't see one of San Francisco's big-name defenders play on Monday.

You see, starting linebacker Dre Greenlaw is currently serving a one-game suspension, which is why he won't play against the Commanders. Now, why did Greenlaw get suspended, you might ask?

In the midst of a heated fracas with the rival Seattle Seahawks in Week 5, Greenlaw headbutted a helmet-less Ernest Jones IV in the face. That is, quite obviously, very dangerous and also against NFL rules. It certainly warrants disciplinary action in the form of suspension for any player.

Here's a clip of the forgettable sequence for Greenlaw and the 49ers:

If there's any consolation for the 49ers, they should be just fine on defense without one of their starting linebackers. It's not as if the Commanders have been lighting it on fire on offense this year. A good game-plan might be enough to help lead San Francisco to another win. Still, they have to hope Greenlaw matures a bit moving forward, or they risk paying the price for his antics in a much bigger game.

Who is Dre Greenlaw's backup on the 49ers

Technically speaking, the 49ers are actually down to their third-string linebacker with both Greenlaw and Greenlaw's primary backup, Garrett Wallow, out. That means rookie fifth-round draft pick Jaden Dugger is expected to make his first career NFL start on Monday night.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni on Eagles allowing Jalen Hurts to play, fly home from London with known blood clot: 'We leave that up to the medical experts'
articles.summary: Sirianni repeatedly cited Eagles "medical experts" when asked Monday about decisions regarding Jalen Hurts' health.
articles.body:
As details continue to emerge regarding Jalen Hurts' blood clot and the decisions by the Philadelphia Eagles to allow him to play and fly overseas with it, so does scrutiny around those decisions.

Head coach Nick Sirianni faced said scrutiny on Monday in the form of a news conference . He was asked repeatedly about how the Eagles went through their decision process in initially managing Hurts' blood clot in his calf. Hurts has since been diagnosed with bilateral pulmonary emboli, which means he has blood clots in both lungs.

Each time he was asked about the topic, Sirianni cited "medical experts" on Philadelphia's staff while declining to divulge details about what conversations were had with whom and how the team's decisions regarding Hurts were made.

"I'm not a medical expert," Sirianni said Monday when asked if the Eagles should have managed Hurts' condition differently. "I lean on our guys in all those situations.

"I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them. It's not just me that has major care for our players. It's them as well."

Sirianni faced this questioning after it was revealed Hurts' diagnosis had worsened since he played and traveled overseas with the blood clot in his calf.

Jalen Hurts' diagnosis worsened after he played in, flew home from London game

The Eagles announced Monday morning in a joint statement with Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn that Hurts had been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. They announced that his "prognosis is very good" and that he's expected to "make a full recovery."

They did not announce a timeline for his return to football, but Hurts will miss the rest of the season, per multiple reports .

News broke later from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, who reported that Hurts had been advised by doctors not to sleep in the 36 hours prior to the game as a medical precaution, and that he acted on that advice. Pelissero's since walked that report back, and, in part due to conflicting reports, it's not clear how much Hurts did or didn't sleep before playing the Jaguars.

But one thing is clear. The Eagles knew about Hurts' blood clot and allowed him to play. They then allowed him to fly home from London to Philadelphia and practice the following Wednesday. They acknowledged as much last week when they issued a statement that an ultrasound revealed the clot on Oct. 10, the Saturday before the Jaguars game.

Only when a followup ultrasound the next week revealed "movement in the small blood clot" did the Eagles announce Hurts' condition and rule him out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

Sirianni's responses provide little clarity

Sirianni was pressed on Monday regarding why the Eagles allowed Hurts to fly from London to Philadelphia when they knew he had a blood clot.

"Again, I'm not a medical expert," Sirianni said. "The same deal there. We get medical information from our guys. We always put the players' health first and foremost in every situation. And that's where we were there."

Pressed on the topic, Sirianni again cited medical experts.

"Guys, I've addressed this," Sirianni continued. "I've talked to you guys about this. Again, the medical experts are there. And I think I've answered this question multiple times. We've put out a statement for you guys to hear."

Sirianni was then asked who was involved in the decisions about managing Hurts' health. His response did not provide an answer.

"I understand that you want the information on this," he continued. "I fully trust the people involved in helping us all make these decisions. And we have great people here. …

"That again goes down to our connection and our team. It kind of feels like you're questioning that. I know you guys have a job to do. I've got the relationship with the players that I have because of the time that we spend together and because of the care that we have for each other."

Hurts has not addressed the subject since Monday's announcement about his worsening medical condition.

articles.title: Could the 49ers' Brock Purdy really win MVP?
articles.summary: Does Brock Purdy have a legit shot at his first MVP? Why the 49ers QB might have a case.
articles.body:
It's still early to make a definitive pick for this year's NFL MVP award, but it sure seems like Brock Purdy might have a rock-solid case. If anything, at this point in late October, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback could actually have the best MVP case of anyone, with his 49ers looking like a bona fide juggernaut.

At the time of this writing (without taking Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders into account), Purdy is:

Fourth in the NFL in yards per attempt (8.4)

Put another way: Purdy has been extremely efficient while also extending and creating big plays for what sure looks like the NFL's best team this season.

I know, I know. Some might say Purdy's candidacy is made possible in the first palce by the incredible coaching and supporting cast surrounding him. Which, on some level, is true. What the stacked 49ers have available for their quarterback would be the envy of almost everyone in the NFL. Still, that feels like a cop-out when considering that every MVP-caliber quarterback is in a great situation. They wouldn't be MVPs if they didn't have a lot of help!

Also, the 49ers are notably older (and a bit more injured) these days. It's no longer a stretch to claim the 26-year-old Purdy might be the straw that stirs the drink for his talented teammates. To be sure, I'm not saying Purdy is the clear MVP favorite by any means. But if there were ever a year to finally crown him, the 2026 season feels like a golden opportunity.

articles.title: Eagles’ Nick Sirianni Does Damage Control After Jalen Hurts Report Emerges
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni answered multiple questions on the latest update on quarterback Jalen Hurts's blood clot. The post Eagles’ Nick...
articles.body:
After losing four consecutive games, Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has to find a way to save his team's season. But first, Sirianni did a different kind of damage control for the Eagles on Monday.

In his first press conference since NFL insider Tom Pelissero's update that Hurts played with no sleep for about 36 hours because of a blood clot, Sirianni faced a barrage of questions on the quarterback.

Throughout the press conference, Sirianni stressed the importance of the Eagles' players health and the trust he has in the organization's medical staff.

"The health of our players is always at the forefront of our minds," said Sirianni on the decision to play Hurts in Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. "We'll leave that up to the medical experts. We always, always care deeply about our players.

"That's when you are completing focused on together and connection, you are always thinking about the well being of your guys and that's what we were in that situation."

Eagles' Nick Sirianni Answers Questions on Jalen Hurts

The Eagles announced in a statement Thursday the team's medical staff diagnosed Hurts with a superficial blood clot in his calf the day before facing the Jacksonville Jaguars on October 11. Pelissero reported on social media Monday that Hurts played in that contest with no sleep for 36 hours out of precaution.

Pelissero presented Hurts playing in Week 5 versus the Jaguars as a dedication to football moment. Social media users, though, took it very differently and began heavily criticizing the Eagles approach to the quarterback's blood clot.

It's important to note that Pelissero has since walked back his initial report slightly . On Monday afternoon, he added this context on X:

"Just spoke to Jalen Hurts ' agent, Nicole Lynn, who clarified that while Hurts was up early Sunday morning getting evaluated at a hospital, he was able to sleep upon rejoining the team and the Eagles set aside a room for him at the stadium," wrote Pelissero . "Videos from the stadium show Hurts coming onto the field just before kickoff and he felt rested enough to play."

But that updated report came out only a few minutes before Sirianni took the podium. The Eagles head coach still faced a lot of difficult questions on Hurts.

Sirianni mostly avoided the questions. Notably, though, he didn't decline the team should have done anything differently.

"Guys, I'm not a medical expert. I lean on our guys in all those situations," said Sirianni. "I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them.

"It's not just me that has major care for our players, it's them as well. We're all there. I'm glad to be part of an organization that cares about the guys the way our guys do."

Sirianni again said he is "not a medical expert" when asked why Hurts was allowed to fly home from London with a blood clot. The reporter who asked that question, The Philadelphia Inquirer's Jeff McLane, pushed to ask a follow-up question, which led to the most tense moment in the press conference.

Sirianni referenced the organization's statement last week and his trust in the team's medical staff as a sufficient enough answer.

Hurts Could Miss Rest of 2026 NFL Season

The Eagles starting quarterback will miss at least four games on injured reserve. But he could be out much longer. Pelissero started his reporting Monday saying the quarterback's blood clots are getting worse.

"Hurts is expected to be sidelined for multiple months after new imaging over the weekend found several blood clots in his lungs.

Hurts is 59-28 as an NFL starting quarterback. He owns a 2-3 record this season. He had eight touchdown passes with three interceptions along with 933 passing yards before landing on IR.

Last season, Hurts made the Pro Bowl with 3,224 passing yards and 25 passing touchdowns. To conclude the 2024 campaign, the quarterback won Super Bowl MVP.

The Eagles placed the quarterback on IR on Saturday. The Eagles then lost to the Carolina Panthers to fall to 2-4 on Sunday.

articles.title: Brock Purdy leads NFL in key passing stat since 2025
articles.summary: Brock Purdy continues to show why he's one of the most effective passers in the NFL.
articles.body:
Brock Purdy has established himself as one of the NFL's most effective quarterbacks at making difficult throws over the middle.

According to ESPN's Nick Wagoner , Purdy leads the league in passing yards on tight-window throws between the hashes since the start of the 2025 season. He is also tied for second in completions on those passes.

ESPN defines a tight-window throw as one in which the intended receiver has less than a yard of separation when the ball arrives. Those passes require quarterbacks to anticipate openings between defenders and deliver the football with precise timing.

Purdy's success in that area is not new. Since becoming the San Francisco 49ers ' starting quarterback in 2022, he ranks second in the NFL in passing yards and yards per attempt on throws between the hashes. He is also tied for third in touchdown passes on those throws among quarterbacks with at least 30 starts during that span.

The numbers help illustrate an important part of Purdy's game in Kyle Shanahan's offense. Rather than simply relying on open receivers, he must consistently fit passes into narrow windows while accounting for linebackers dropping into coverage and defensive backs closing from the secondary.

Purdy has continued to produce at a high level in 2026. Through five games, he has completed 69% of his passes for 1,196 yards and 13 touchdowns against two interceptions, posting a 119.3 passer rating.

Purdy's ability to attack the middle of the field provides another measurable example of why he has emerged as one of the league's most productive quarterbacks. His efficiency on difficult throws has become a defining feature of his performance in San Francisco's offense.

articles.title: When is Nick Bosa coming back to the 49ers?
articles.summary: Here's what we know about Nick Bosa's status for the 49ers moving forward.
articles.body:
It's still technically early, but the San Francisco 49ers sure seem like the NFL's best team . That's the only reasonable conclusion for a squad with an undefeated record and a +61-point differential entering a home Monday night matchup with the Washington Commanders . The 49ers ' tremendous all-around success so far is made all the more impressive given that they've been missing one of their best players for most of the season to date .

I'm talking, of course, about former Defensive Player of the Year Nick Bosa. The veteran defensive end has been dealing with a calf injury since a Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins . The 49ers have, quite obviously, already ruled out the talisman defender for Monday night's matchup as they continue to exercise caution with the recovery and health of one of their most important pieces for a possible Super Bowl run.

That begs the question. After missing three straight games, when will Bosa finally make his return to the 49ers' lineup? Based on the tenor of reporting around his injury, it sure seems like his comeback could be imminent, perhaps even as soon as the 49ers' Week 7 road date with the Atlanta Falcons next Sunday.

Of course, soft-tissue injuries can be very finicky. If the 49ers wanted to ensure Bosa was as close to himself as possible when he returns, holding him out of the Falcons game with a bye week right after would make a lot of sense. In light of that, a Week 9 return in a home game against the Las Vegas Raiders feels like a prudent big-picture move for Bosa and the 49ers with their January (and February) goals. That timeline would also give nearly two months of recovery time for his injury, which seems like a best-case scenario at face value.

The 49ers have survived this long in the early season without Bosa. What's another week or two as they try to finally win a Super Bowl during the Kyle Shanahan era?

articles.title: Report suggests Broncos QB Bo Nix is worried about injuring his ankle again
articles.summary: James Palmer has suggested the Broncos believe Bo Nix is still worried about his ankle, and that is holding the QB back.
articles.body:
Six games into the 2026 NFL season, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix ranks 32nd in the NFL with an average of 5.6 yards per passing attempt.

Nix's struggles and inability (or unwillingness) to throw the ball downfield have been well-documented this season, and the QB was asked about it following the team's 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks last Thursday.

"I don't understand why we can't really push the ball vertically right now," Nix said. "Defenses are just sitting back there hanging out. We're just going to keep running the football. Hopefully you have to find ways to get more out of it."

Some fans and pundits have speculated that Nix's struggles are related to the ankle injury Nix suffered during the NFL playoffs last season. Not so much the physical fallout , but Nix's ability to get over the injury mentally.

When asked if Nix is struggling to mentally move past his injury during his Monday conference call, Broncos coach Sean Payton essentially sidestepped the question, saying the QB has done a good job overcoming adversity in his career.

"All the other things relative to the mental toughness, the mental fortitude — this is a tough league," Payton said . "We hit every aspect, and I think that's one of the things that attracted us to Bo in the beginning is we had seen his ability to climb through adversity. It's not just Bo that feels that. Right now, offensively, I feel that, our players feel that and we'll improve."

Publicly, Payton didn't suggest Nix is struggling to get over his injury mentally. Meanwhile, somebody (presumably within the organization) has leaked to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video that the club believes Nix is playing "a bit gun shy."

"[T]here is a difference with Nix in 2026, where Nix is focused on not losing the game more than winning the game," Palmer tweeted on Monday . "Don't turn the ball over. Don't be the reason why we lose the game. That's kind of manifested in his mind to the point that the conservative approach has become an issue on the field."

Palmer's lengthy tweet also included this:

Nix is healthy, and the ankle is fine . But returning from an injury is also not cut and dry and takes time. The Broncos want Nix to run it more and they're seeing a player that is a bit gun shy right now. If you look at the runs that Denver has dialed up, a lot of them he's looking for the sidelines and he's looking for a way to get down as soon as possible. He's not looking for the extra yards or the needed yards in key situations. It's been frustrating.

Palmer later suggested that Nix is "seeing ghosts at times," and the team is "obviously concerned with the funk he's currently stuck in." And this is perhaps the most notable part of the report : "They'd love to see him take a couple of big hits and realize he's not going to get hurt, the ankle is good, remember you're a tough football player."

Assuming Palmer's information came straight from the team, that seems to be an admission that the club believes Nix is in his head about coming back from last season's ankle injury. That's not surprising, given that many fans and pundits came to the same conclusion.

This week, Nix will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that allows 8.6 yards per passing attempt, most in the NFL. Palmer noted that "one big game" could get Nix going again. Fans in Denver can only hope that Nix gets back on track and regains his confidence in Arizona this week.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' brother shares sweet family moment at Steelers game
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers posed for a photo with his brother, niece, and nephews.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers' brother, Luke Rodgers, shared a snapshot of a special moment with their family over the weekend. Luke came to support Aaron during the Pittsburgh Steelers matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 18.

"Last weekend was pretty special," Luke captioned the photos with his brother and children at the game.

Aaron commented on the post, " Planes, trains, and renegade! also misspelled cakes."

"The best weekend!" Luke's wife, Aimee, commented on the post. "Also, I want to be sure everyone knows, I cut a huge slit down that poncho, so Bella was only covered by my hand and not by any plastic! I feel like I need to be proactive about that."

The photos showed the family wrapped in plastic ponchos to combat the rainy and windy weather during the game. Aaron posed with his niece Evie and nephew Jack on the sidelines. Luke and Aimee have three children after recently welcoming their baby girl in August.

The post also showed some clips of the children cheering on their uncle in the suite as they rocked their Steelers gear. Luke added some at-home moments as well, celebrating a birthday and Aaron playing with trains with Jack.

The photo follows Aaron's own post with his parents, Luke, and his niece and nephew in July. The Steelers quarterback spoke about what it meant to him to have his family by his side after a years-long estrangement.

"I'm happy to be reunited, and that part of my life is a really beautiful addition, and I gotta give my wife a lot of credit for — not that she was pushing me because she never was — but just the way she loves and supports me, having her by my side throughout this process has been really special, and I miss those relationships," he recalled in conversation with NFL Network's Kyle Brandt.

"It's been really beautiful to reconnect with them — all of them," he said. "I got to spend a long weekend recently with my parents … my brother and his sweet wife and their incredible two kids. I got to be an uncle."

While Luke shared photos of the family, Aaron revealed that he will "never" post them again .

"There's been a narrative out there," he said, referencing news about the strained relationship with his family per USA Today. "There's not been a lot of information that's truthful about it. And I think that the personal life should stay personal and private."

"But I feel like it was part of the full-circle to just one time post something, and never again," he added. "So that that narrative can finally be put to rest."

This is Aaron's last season in the NFL after 22 seasons. The Steelers' next game will be on Sunday, Oct. 25 against the New Orleans Saints.

articles.title: After slow start in loss to Bears, Penix and Falcons have urgency to turn their season around
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Another slow start to a game has left the Atlanta Falcons with an urgent need to reverse their slow start to the season.Two straight losses ha...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Another slow start to a game has left the Atlanta Falcons with an urgent need to reverse their slow start to the season.

Two straight losses have left the Falcons (2-4) two games under .500. It's a familiar challenge for a team looking to end a streak of eight straight losing seasons.

The Falcons trailed 14-0 in Sunday's 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears before recording a first down. They opened the game with two straight three-and-outs following long touchdown drives by the Bears. Chicago dominated the first quarter the way Bears fans took over Atlanta's home stadium.

"Certainly our goal as a team is to start fast," coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday.

Responsibility for failing to come close to that goal fell equally on the offense and defense.

The Falcons' defense couldn't slow quarterback Caleb Williams and the Bears' offense.

Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. led only one scoring drive in the first half and the Falcons trailed 31-7 before finally demonstrating offensive potential while running their two-minute offense in the fourth quarter. For most of the game, Penix struggled against pressure from the Bears, failing to take advantage of opportunities created by blitzes.

Penix was sacked five times and fumbled twice, losing one.

Stefanski knows other teams will take note of the Bears' game plan on defense.

"I think the name of the game in the NFL is when they pressure you as an offense, you have to make them pay," Stefanski said. "We didn't do that enough yesterday and that's on all of us. ... You have to look at those as an opportunity if teams are going to all-out blitz you in a given game. So we know this league can be a copycat league. So you'll see if that continues to be the trend."

Penix missed the first two games of the season while completing his recovery from a torn ACL in his left knee that ended his 2025 season. The Falcons were 0-2 with Cooper Rush as the fill-in starter. Rush was released on Monday, when the Falcons signed veteran Andy Dalton .

Tua Tagovailoa is expected to keep his job as Penix's backup, at least for this week as Dalton learns the system. Rookie Jack Strand's role as a developmental player won't change as long as the Falcons keep four quarterbacks.

Atlanta's fourth-quarter comeback attempt allowed tight end Kyle Pitts to show why he should have been better utilized earlier in the game. Pitts had scoring catches of 10 and 5 yards in the final quarter. He had five catches for 60 yards and has a combined three scoring receptions in the last two games after having none in the first four.

Rookie Zachariah Branch lost two fumbles on returns. He misjudged a fair catch attempt on a second-quarter punt and fumbled a kickoff return late in the third quarter. Branch had a catch for a 2-point conversion in the final quarter.

Cornerback A.J. Terrell, who was placed on injured reserve following a groin injury in the first quarter of a 34-3 home loss to Carolina in Week 2, is eligible to return this week after missing four games.

"It's trending that way, but let's get through the next couple of days," Stefanski said when asked about Terrell playing this week.

The return of Terrell, the older brother of rookie nickel back Avieon Terrell, would be a big boost after the Falcons gave up 305 passing yards to Williams.

Bijan Robinson had 16 or more carries in each of the first five games and entered the weekend leading the NFL with 580 rushing yards. Thanks to the big early deficit, the Falcons couldn't maintain their normal commitment to the running game and Robinson had season-low totals of nine carries for 61 yards.

Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was at the team practice facility on Monday after he left the field on a stretcher with a neck injury in the third quarter on Sunday.

Stefanski said it was too early to project Daniels' status for this week but said he was grateful for "all positive news." The Falcons announced Sunday that Daniels was alert and had movement in all his extremities. After being taken to a hospital for further evaluation, he returned to the locker room after the game.

"So I feel very, very fortunate that he got the treatment he got," Stefanski said. "But also that we feel really good about where he is."

Stefanski had no updates on ILB Divine Deablo (arm), CB Avieon Terrell (left shoulder) or DB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring).

Minus-8: Robinson had two catches for a combined loss of 8 yards. On the Falcons' opening drive, he caught a pass from Penix behind the line of scrimmage and was dropped for a loss of 5 yards. On the second drive, Penix again tried a quick pass to Robinson behind the line, losing 3 yards.

The Falcons, 0-3 at home, will try again for their first win of the season at Mercedes-Benz Stadium when the San Francisco 49ers visit on Sunday.

articles.title: When Giants’ J.J. McCarthy could start for New York, according to Ian Rapoport
articles.summary: With the decision for the New York Giants to go with either J.J. McCarthy or Jameis Winston as the team’s starting quarterback, the conversation stems from t...
articles.body:
With the decision for the New York Giants to go with either J.J. McCarthy or Jameis Winston as the team's starting quarterback, the conversation stems from the 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. While McCarthy's time is seemingly coming for the Giants, this NFL insider discusses when that could be the case.

In the loss to New Orleans, Winston threw for 152 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, leading New York to put McCarthy in the game after trading for him from the Minnesota Vikings in late September.

Coming into the game in the fourth quarter, he showed flashes, throwing for 243 yards with a touchdown and interception, with Ian Rapoport saying to Jeremy Fowler on the NFL Network that they could wait a week because of the Houston Texans' defense.

"I would not expect a decision until the New York Giants really have time to kind of let this breathe and really just figure out the various factors at stake, and one of those factors…they face the Houston Texans' pass rush," Rapoport said. "They are good. Now, the defense hasn't been quite as stingy as it has in the past, but Will Anderson playing like one of the top players in the NFL, regardless of position. Danielle Hunter is balling as per usual, and that be the situation you would put J.J. McCarthy out in, and while not knowing how up to speed he is on the protections and essentially keeping him out of harm's way."

J.J. McCarthy to see "significant snaps" for the Giants

While McCarthy may not be starting for the Giants on Sunday against the Texans, "significant snaps" are coming for the 23-year-old this season.

"Here's what we learned yesterday in the fourth quarter for the New York Giants. J.J. McCarthy's time is coming. Whether it's this week, whether it's after the bye, we don't know that for sure," Rapoport said. "J.J. McCarthy is going to play significant snaps for the Giants this season."

At any rate, it remains to be seen who New York head coach John Harbaugh picks to start Sunday against Houston.
